messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick thread on cross-team calibration logistics for this cycle. We made a few process tweaks to reduce bias and speed up the meetings — pls skim.

Ethan (Eng Manager): TL;DR what changed vs last cycle?

Maya (People Ops): Short list: 1) pre-calibration packet required (no anchors = no scoring), 2) anonymized snippet standard, 3) hard cap on meeting time per team, 4) dissent capture & 48h appeal window. Details below.

Lina (Product Manager): Pre-calibration packet = what goes inside exactly?

Maya (People Ops): Packet = 3 anonymized anchors (A/B/C), context line (role + tenure), manager rationale (max 150 words), and the raw evidence snippet (no names). Use the template: https://rwd.in/cali-packet. If packet missing, we defer that employee to the "late anchors" slot.

Cal (Reviewer): How strict is anonymization? We often need a tiny context hint to judge scope.

Maya (People Ops): Keep role + team-size and project scale only. No names, no repo paths, no specific customer IDs. Example allowed context: "senior backend IC, 18-month tenure, led infra perf work impacting 3 services." Forbidden: "repo: infra-x, mentored Alex". This is enforced by the import pipeline.

Ethan (Eng Manager): Meeting time cap? Our team had long calibration debates last time.

Maya (People Ops): Each team gets 12 minutes per tranche of 8 packets. Use the timer in the calibration agenda. If discussion needs >12m, note the concern and it goes to the follow-up queue (48h deep-dive slot). This keeps round-robin moving.

Nate (People Ops): Also adding a new "anchor quality" flag in the import: green/yellow/red. If anchor flagged red by two reviewers, we drop it from the primary calibration and use it in the canary deep-dive.

Cal (Reviewer): Dissent capture & appeals flow? Curious about how we log disagreements for HR/comp reviewers.

Maya (People Ops): During calibration, if a reviewer disagrees with the majority by 2+ points, they mark "disagree" and provide a 1-line rationale. People-ops collects these into the dissent log. Managers have 48h after calibration to submit an appeal with new evidence; appeals are limited to process errors or new substantive evidence. Appeals are reviewed by the calibration steward panel.

Lina (Product Manager): Who's on the steward panel? Can managers request a particular steward if conflict?

Maya (People Ops): Steward panel = rotating mix (People Ops rep, senior eng manager, senior product manager). If conflict with any steward, recuse by sending a DM to people-ops and we'll swap to the alternate.

Ethan (Eng Manager): Any changes to rating scale? We had confusion about 4 vs 5-levels.

Maya (People Ops): We're standardizing to a 5-level scale this cycle with clear anchors for each level in the packet template. Level 4 = "exceeds" with sustained impact; Level 3 = "meets"; Level 5 = "exceptional". Packets must map behaviors to anchor bullets. Calibration slides include explicit examples.

Cal (Reviewer): Timezones — calibration meetings span NA & EU. How do we ensure fair participation?

Nate (People Ops): We're running two identical calibration windows per tranche: one West-friendly and one East-friendly. The panel will merge outcomes; if outcomes diverge by >1 point median, we schedule a short cross-window sync. Use the timezone availability field in the packet.

Lina (Product Manager): What about conflict of interest (manager that is also a reviewer for same team)?

Maya (People Ops): Conflict rule: reviewers cannot be assigned to calibrate packets from their direct reports or anyone on their skip-level ladder. If an accidental assignment shows up, flag it in Slack thread and we reassign immediately. The import will auto-detect org overlaps and warn.

PR-Bot: Reminder: calibration packet imports close Fri 17:00 PT. Auto-notify to all reviewers 48h before meeting.

Ethan (Eng Manager): If an anchor is removed for quality, can manager resubmit?

Maya (People Ops): Yes — if anchor flagged red, manager will be notified and given a 24h window to resubmit a cleaned/edited anchor or request it go to the deep-dive queue. Resubmissions must address anonymization and length requirements.

Cal (Reviewer): How will people-ops share post-calibration outputs? I want to see final medians & dissent logs for my team.

Nate (People Ops): We'll publish a per-team calibration summary (median score, flagged dissents, appeals status) within 48h of the meeting. Managers receive a CSV export and a short narrative for calibration outcomes.

Lina (Product Manager): Any quick tips to avoid anchors being tossed?

Maya (People Ops): Keep anchors concise (max 200 words), anonymize strictly, include one clear impact metric, and attach supporting artifacts (PR link, customer impact note) in a single zipped appendix (no names). Use the template and you're usually fine.

Ethan (Eng Manager): Great. I'll run a mini dry-run with my team this week and use the template.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks all 44d If you hit an import error, paste the import log into this thread and tag @people-ops. We'll triage within the day.
